results.notes: Same offline token spent again from another device — the signature & reuse rules should refuse it outright.
Amount at 94% of the reserved cap with huge merchant deviation — a tampered receipt / overspend attempt.
Amount bumped well above the merchant normal after signing; crypto re-verification catches the forged canonical string too.
New device with zero history: fraud-service's low-signal guard (FraudScoringService) downgrades any would-be APPROVE to HOLD_FOR_REVIEW — a brand-new device never auto-approves.
Identical payload seen before (replayed submission) — idempotency and duplicate rules refuse it.
Dozens of payments in a few minutes — classic mule velocity.

Payment stayed offline past the token's working life and surfaced near expiry. The model scores this strongly (>= 0.75) and rejects — stricter than a mere hold, which is the safe call for long-offline.
